recentItems.title: Why UK troops need to ‘hit back’ against Russia to stop war
recentItems.description:

recentItems.title: I was told never to play again - now I'm Army Rugby head coach
recentItems.description:
The Army men's senior rugby union team have a new head coach, and he's come a long way to get here.

Find out more about his story, including how he was told his rugby career had to be over after a car crash but returned to playing anyway.

recentItems.title: British troops caught in 'The war of losers'
recentItems.description:
Iran’s strikes on US military bases in the Middle East are a blunt reminder that British servicemen and women deployed in the region face real risks.

Professor Michael Clarke assesses the dangers while former Royal Navy Commander Tom Sharpe explains the options for British ships which had been standing by for a possible protection role in the Strait of Hormuz.

UK and US bases are often co-located, including Bahrain, where a US Navy Admiral has told his personnel they won’t be returning “any time soon”.

Retired Lieutenant General Sir Simon Mayall, who led the creation of the Royal Navy base in Bahrain, explains the potential impact of a facility designed to operate independently of the US but also primarily intended for joint operations.

Sian Grzeszczyk Melbourne, presents, with expert analysis from Professor Michael Clarke.

recentItems.title: Is the Army preparing to recruit more 16 year-olds?
recentItems.description:
More teenagers in the UK could join the Armed Forces if the government follows through on early plans to create a second dedicated training establishment for 16- and 17-year-old recruits.

Each year, roughly one in four recruits to the British Army are under the age of 18.

Known as Junior Soldiers, they complete their Phase One training with parental consent at the Army Foundation College in Harrogate, North Yorkshire.
